Cleaning Contract Summary

Supersedes the South-West-only version effective 1 June 2025. The same contractor's national framework agreement now covers all regions.

Site	Contractor	Frequency
All sites, all regions	CleanCo National Ltd (successor to CleanCo South West Ltd's framework)	Daily

assuming it is too minor to matter.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a resident specifically prefers a corridor or communal light left on overnight for their own comfort or orientation, this preference is accommodated even though it runs against the general energy efficiency actions guidance, since a resident's individual wellbeing takes priority over a general energy-saving measure.

Local and regional variations

A larger site such as Harbour View has a more complex heating zoning system, and its facilities team monitors zone-by-zone usage rather than a single site-wide reading, reflecting its greater complexity.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This policy works alongside the Health and Safety Policy (ensuring an energy efficiency action never compromises safety) and the Business Continuity Plan Summary (relevant where a utility fault becomes a wider supply issue).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates that the substance is unchanged from the previous version, only the section heading. A resident who becomes anxious in full darkness asks for their corridor light to remain on overnight. Staff accommodate this request even though it means one additional light stays on beyond what the energy efficiency actions guidance suggests, exactly as they would have under the previous heading.

Frequently asked questions

**Why was the heading renamed?** A review found 'energy efficiency actions' better reflects the practical, action-oriented nature of the section than the more abstract 'energy saving measures'; the underlying content did not change. **Does turning off lighting overnight apply to every area of a site?** No, safety and resident access lighting always remains on; only genuinely non-essential lighting is affected.

Training and competency

Night staff are shown which lighting is considered non-essential at their specific site during induction, since this varies slightly by site layout.

Monitoring and compliance

Facilities reviews reported heating faults and their resolution time monthly, and monitors overall site energy usage against expected patterns.

Record keeping and retention

Reported faults and their resolution are retained per the Records Retention Schedule.

Approval and review history

This policy was approved by the Chief Executive on 1 April 2025 and this version took effect, superseding the earlier heading.
